daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿أَلْهاكُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿التَّكاثُرُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive. ﴿زُرْتُمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْمَقابِرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from the implied (muḍmara) an after ḥattā and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿كَلَّا سَوْفَ﴾ a particle of deterrence and rebuke (radʿ wa-zajr), and sawfa is for the future. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of deterrence and rebuke (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿لَوْ﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to اليقين; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which has been omitted because of the succession of like letters (tawālī al-amthāl), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْجَحِيمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the response to the omitted oath, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّها﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which has been omitted because of the succession of like letters (tawālī al-amthāl); the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and hā is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ﴾ عين is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. «a seeing of the eye» (ruʾyata ʿayn), and it is muḍāf to اليقين; the clause is the response to the omitted oath, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَتُسْئَلُنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which has been omitted; the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two sukūns (iltiqāʾ al-sākinayn), is its fāʿil (agent), and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis (nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it. [Translator's note: the source calls the wāw the fāʿil, although the verb is passive; strictly it would be the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). Translated as written.] ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) annexed to one like it. ﴿عَنِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

farraa:1-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلْهَاكُمُ ٱلتَّكَّاثُرُ﴾.
It was revealed concerning two clans of Quraysh who vied in boasting over which of them was more numerous; they were Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm. Banū ʿAbd Manāf outnumbered [147/b] Banū Sahm, and Banū Sahm said: Wrongdoing destroyed [many of] us in the Jāhiliyya, so count us against one another with the living and the dead. Then Banū Sahm outnumbered them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿أَلْهَاكُمُ ٱلتَّكَّاثُرُ﴾, until you mentioned [even] the dead. Then He said to them: ﴿كَلاَّ﴾: the matter is not as you [hold]; and He said: ﴿سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾. The Arabs sometimes repeat a word for severity and intimidation, and this is of that kind.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عِلْمَ ٱلْيَقِينِ﴾.
Like His word: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾. The meaning in it is: if you knew with a certain knowledge.

farraa:6-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ﴾.
﴿ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا﴾: [said] twice, also for severity. ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ ٱلْيَقِينِ﴾: with the eye [of one who is present], you not being absent. This is the reading of the generality — the people of Medina, the people of Kufa and the people of Basra — with fatḥa on the tāʾ in both words.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us; he said:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl narrated to me from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read: "لَتُرَوُن الْجَحِيمَ، ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها", with ḍamma on the first tāʾ and fatḥa on the second. The first is more in keeping with the speech of the Arabs, because it is [repetition for] severity, so its wording ought not to differ. Do you not see His word: ﴿سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُون، ثُمَّ كَلاَّ سوْف تَعلَمون﴾? And His word, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْر يُسْراً، إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرا﴾.
And of [repetition for] severity is His word in the surah: ﴿قُلْ يَأَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ، لاَ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدونَ﴾, repeated: it is repeated in it while being a single meaning. Had you given the tāʾ ḍamma in the second, as you gave it ḍamma in the first, it would have been a good way.

farraa:8-8.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لَتُسْأَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ﴾.
He said: it is security and health. Al-Kalbī mentioned, with his chain of transmission, that the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were out on some business and came back hungry, and they went in to a man of the Anṣār and got dates and cold water. When they came out, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: Indeed, you will be asked about these and about this. They said: Then what is the thanks for it, O Messenger of Allah? He said: That you say: Praise be to Allah. [148/a]
And it is mentioned in this report that the Prophet ﷺ said: (Three things the Muslim will not be asked about: food that keeps his back upright, a garment that covers his nakedness, and a house that shelters him from heat and cold).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Takāthur
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألْهاكُمُ التَّكاثُرُ﴾ ("rivalry in increase has distracted you"): that is, rivalry in increase of wealth and children has occupied you away from obedience to Allah.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿حَتّى زُرْتُمُ المَقابِرَ﴾ ("until you visited the graves"): that is, until death overtook you in that state. It has come in the exegesis that two clans of the Arabs, Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm, vied in boasting and in numbers. Banū ʿAbd Manāf boasted over Banū Sahm by counting the living; so Banū Sahm said: "Then mention the dead!" And Banū Sahm outnumbered them, after Banū ʿAbd Manāf had outnumbered Banū Sahm.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿كَلا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ ("nay, you will come to know"): ”كَلّا“ is a deterrent and a warning. The meaning is: "Rivalry in increase is not the matter that they ought to be upon; what they ought to be upon is obedience to Allah and belief in His Prophet ﷺ."

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ اليَقِينِ﴾ ("nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty"): the meaning is: "If you knew the thing with its true knowledge and turned your understanding toward it, you would have desisted." Then He said: ﴿لَتَرَوُنَّ الجَحِيمَ﴾ [al-Takāthur: 6] ("you will surely see Hellfire"), as He said: ﴿وَإنْ مِنكم إلا وارِدُها﴾ [Maryam: 71] ("and there is none of you but will come to it"). The reading is ”لَتَرَوُنَّ“ with ḍamma on the wāw, without hamza: the wāw was given ḍamma because of its being vowelless together with the vowelless nūn. Some read it with hamza: ”لَتَرَؤُنَّ“. The grammarians dislike putting hamza on the wāw, because its ḍamma is not inherent (ghayr lāzima), since it was vowelled only because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; whereas they do put hamza on a wāw whose ḍamma is inherent, as in ”أدْؤُرٌ“, plural of ”دارٌ“ ("house"): so ”أدْؤُرٌ“ with hamza and ”أدْوُرٌ“ without hamza are both permissible, and you have the choice between them. But as for ”لَتَرَؤُنَّ“ [and] ”ثُمَّ لَتَرَؤُنَّها“, the grammarians choose only leaving out the hamza. It was also read: ”لَتُرَؤُنَّ الجَحِيمَ“ ("you will surely be shown Hellfire"), as a passive (ʿalā mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu).

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ لَتُسْألُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ﴾ ("then you will surely be asked on that Day about the pleasures"): that is, on the Day of Resurrection, about everything enjoyed in this world. It has come in the ḥadīth «that the Prophet, peace be upon him, together with a group of his Companions, ate dates — and it is related: unripe dates (busr) — and drank water after them, and he said: ”اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أطْعَمَنا وسَقانا وجَعَلَنا مُسْلِمِينَ“ ("Praise be to Allah, Who fed us, gave us drink and made us Muslims")». And it has come that among the things the servant will not be asked about are: clothing that covers his nakedness, food by which he keeps his back upright, and a place that shelters him from heat and cold.
